subject.title: Session maintenance: durable conversation pointers have no retention path, and maxEntries below the durable-pointer count causes permanent per-write cap churn

question: Should inactive durable external conversation pointers remain indefinitely protected, or should OpenClaw add an explicit retention lifecycle for them after the no-churn repair lands?
rationale: The repeated futile cap pass is a source-backed defect, but deleting durable thread, group, or channel pointers changes the documented conversation-continuity contract and requires a deliberate product policy.

options.title: Split repair and policy
options.body: Land a bounded no-churn fix now, then decide durable-pointer retention separately with explicit inactivity and re-entry semantics.

options.title: Retain indefinitely
options.body: Keep durable pointers permanently exempt and treat `maxEntries` as a cap only on removable synthetic rows, with clear diagnostics when protected rows exceed it.

options.title: Add durable retention
options.body: Define a documented age or inactivity policy that can retire durable pointers while preserving safe conversation restart and routing behavior.

recommendation.title: Split repair and policy
recommendation.body: Land a bounded no-churn fix now, then decide durable-pointer retention separately with explicit inactivity and re-entry semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The adjacent merged session-retention work shows Josh directing the policy boundary between fixed internal cleanup and public retention configuration.
